title: Opening Up Closings
abstract: Analyzes how conversational participants collaboratively bring interactions to a close, developing an account based on sequential organization, turn structure, topic organization, and the conditional relevance of conversational actions.

title: A Simplest Systematics for the Organization of Turn-Taking for Conversation
abstract: Presents a locally managed and interactionally controlled model of conversational turn taking, providing foundational machinery for understanding how responses are sequentially related to preceding conversational actions.

title: Questions in Montague English
abstract: Develops a formal semantic treatment of questions in which questions are associated with sets of possible answers, providing an influential foundation for later work on answerhood and question resolution.

title: Syntax and semantics of questions
abstract: Provides a compositional semantic analysis of questions and their possible answers, establishing machinery that later work uses to characterize when propositions answer or partially resolve a question.

title: Studies on the Semantics of Questions and the Pragmatics of Answers
abstract: Develops a systematic formal account of question semantics and the pragmatics of answers, including how propositions partition possibilities and contribute to resolving information requested by a question.

title: Resolving questions, I
abstract: Develops a formal account of how questions are resolved in discourse, connecting question meaning, contextual information, and the semantic contribution of responses.

title: Resolving questions, II
abstract: Extends the formal theory of question resolution to additional discourse phenomena and clarifies how conversational context constrains what counts as an appropriate resolution of a question.

title: Questions in Dialogue
abstract: Integrates question semantics with discourse structure and dialogue interpretation, examining how discourse relations and participants' information states constrain the interpretation of questions and answers.

title: Information Structure: Towards an integrated formal theory of pragmatics
abstract: Develops a Questions Under Discussion account of discourse organization in which questions structure conversational goals and propositions are relevant insofar as they address the current question under discussion.

title: Discourse Deixis: Reference to Discourse Segments
venue: 26th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
abstract: Presents a computational account of discourse-deictic expressions whose referents are interpretations associated with portions of prior discourse rather than ordinary nominal entities.

title: Structure and ostension in the interpretation of discourse deixis
abstract: Examines demonstrative expressions that refer to interpretations of one or more clauses and argues that discourse structure constrains which prior discourse segments are available for deictic reference.

title: Reference to Abstract Objects in Discourse
abstract: Develops a semantic theory of reference to abstract entities such as propositions, facts, events, and situations, providing a foundational treatment of how discourse introduces and subsequently refers to such objects.

title: Dialogue Acts, Synchronizing Units, and Anaphora Resolution
abstract: Studies anaphora in spontaneous dialogue and proposes an account linking dialogue structure and synchronizing units to the interpretation of anaphoric expressions, including references whose antecedents are not simple nominal entities.

title: Resolving Pronominal Reference to Abstract Entities
venue: Proceedings of the 40th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
abstract: Introduces a computational approach for resolving pronouns that refer to abstract entities as well as ordinary individuals, explicitly constructing candidate abstract referents from preceding discourse.

title: Annotating Abstract Pronominal Anaphora in the DAD Project
abstract: Describes annotation of abstract pronominal anaphora in Danish and Italian data, covering antecedents realized by verb phrases, clauses, and larger discourse segments and referents such as events, situations, and propositions.

title: Annotating Discourse Anaphora
abstract: Develops corpus annotation guidelines for discourse-deictic anaphora, including identification of antecedent material and semantic referent types, using German discourse data with speaker turns.

title: Antecedent and Referent Types of Abstract Pronominal Anaphora
venue: Beyond Semantics: Corpus-based Investigations of Pragmatic and Discourse Phenomena
abstract: Analyzes abstract pronominal anaphora with respect to syntactic antecedent types, semantic referent types, and antecedent distance, including clauses and discourse segments referring to events, situations, properties, and propositions.

title: The Use of Parallel and Comparable Data for Analysis of Abstract Anaphora in German and English
abstract: Uses parallel and comparable English-German data to study features useful for abstract-anaphora analysis and resolution, with attention to discourse-deictic antecedents and cross-linguistic evidence.

title: Resolving Shell Nouns
abstract: Addresses automatic resolution of shell nouns to the clauses or other textual material that supply their semantic content, treating the problem as locating potentially non-nominal antecedent spans.

title: A Mention-Ranking Model for Abstract Anaphora Resolution
abstract: Formulates abstract-anaphora resolution as mention ranking and learns to score candidate antecedent spans for abstract anaphors, combining neural representation learning with training data derived from shell-noun constructions.

title: Detecting and Resolving Shell Nouns in German
abstract: Presents a system that first detects shell-noun constructions and then links shell nouns to textual content phrases, including explicit modeling of candidates for which no valid content link should be made.

title: Anaphora With Non-nominal Antecedents in Computational Linguistics: a Survey
abstract: Surveys computational research on anaphors whose antecedents are clauses, sentences, or discourse segments and whose referents may be propositions, events, facts, or situations, covering terminology, annotation, datasets, and resolution methods.

title: Resolving abstract anaphors in Spanish discourse: Underspecification and mereological structures
abstract: Examines abstract anaphora in Spanish where several preceding propositions or eventualities may contribute to the interpretation, using discourse structure and mereological relations to represent complex abstract referents.

title: The CODI-CRAC 2021 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis in Dialogue
abstract: Defines shared tasks for anaphora, bridging, and discourse-deixis resolution over multiple conversational datasets, including end-to-end identification of discourse-deictic links rather than assuming ordinary entity antecedents.

title: Neural Anaphora Resolution in Dialogue
abstract: Describes neural systems for the CODI-CRAC dialogue shared task, including a discourse-deixis component that identifies and resolves anaphoric references to prior discourse material.

title: The CODI-CRAC 2021 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis Resolution in Dialogue: A Cross-Team Analysis
abstract: Analyzes systems submitted to the dialogue anaphora shared task across identity, bridging, and discourse-deixis resolution, comparing modeling choices and error patterns relevant to selecting discourse antecedents.

title: The CODI-CRAC 2022 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis in Dialogue
abstract: Extends the dialogue reference-resolution shared task with new test data and subtasks for directly detecting anaphoric relations, including discourse-deictic links in conversational data.

title: Anaphora Resolution in Dialogue: System Description (CODI-CRAC 2022 Shared Task)
abstract: Describes a dialogue anaphora system whose discourse-deixis component combines antecedent resolution with prediction of the anaphoric expression's type, alongside related bridging and identity-resolution components.

title: Neural Anaphora Resolution in Dialogue Revisited
abstract: Revisits neural dialogue anaphora resolution using a span-based architecture and systematic hyperparameter optimization across identity, bridging, and discourse-deixis tracks.

title: End-to-End Neural Discourse Deixis Resolution in Dialogue
abstract: Presents an end-to-end neural model for discourse-deixis resolution in dialogue that identifies discourse-deictic anaphors and their antecedent spans rather than relying on gold anaphor or antecedent boundaries.

title: Discourse parsing for multi-party chat dialogues
abstract: Addresses discourse parsing of multi-party chat by predicting which discourse units attach to which earlier units and which discourse relations hold between them, rather than assuming adjacent or gold argument pairs.

title: Discourse Structure and Dialogue Acts in Multiparty Dialogue: the STAC Corpus
abstract: Introduces the STAC corpus of multiparty chats annotated with elementary discourse units, discourse links, and relations under Segmented Discourse Representation Theory, including interleaved conversational threads and response relations.

title: Molweni: A Challenge Multiparty Dialogues-based Machine Reading Comprehension Dataset with Discourse Structure
abstract: Introduces a large multiparty-dialogue corpus with discourse-dependency annotations and question-answering data, including relations such as question-answer pairs, clarification, and correction as well as answerable and unanswerable questions.

title: Improving Dialogue Discourse Parsing via Reply-to Structures of Addressee Recognition
abstract: Improves dialogue discourse parsing by jointly exploiting reply-to structure from addressee recognition, while predicting discourse attachments and relation labels on STAC and Molweni.

title: Dialogue Discourse Parsing as Generation: A Sequence-to-Sequence LLM-based Approach
abstract: Formulates dialogue discourse parsing as sequence generation, producing discourse structures and relation labels for graph-structured conversational data such as STAC and Molweni.

title: Detection of Question-Answer Pairs in Email Conversations
abstract: Identifies questions and their corresponding answers across email conversations by combining thread structure and textual evidence, directly addressing semantic response linkage in asynchronous workplace-style communication.

title: Agreement and Disputes in Dialogue
abstract: Develops a discourse-semantic account of agreement and dispute based on relational speech acts and shared public commitments, allowing responses to alter commitments associated with earlier discourse content.

title: Agreement, Disputes and Commitments in Dialogue
abstract: Formalizes agreement and disagreement through public commitments and rhetorical relations, accounting for explicit and implicit agreement and for the particular discourse content over which interlocutors' commitments interact.

title: OK or not OK? Commitments in acknowledgments and corrections
abstract: Develops a semantics of acknowledgments and corrections using structured public commitments, explaining how such responses accept, modify, or correct content contributed by preceding discourse.

title: Event-building through Role-filling and Anaphora Resolution
venue: 29th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
abstract: Explores event representations in discourse and the interaction between event construction and anaphora resolution, including cases in which event descriptions provide antecedents for subsequent reference.

title: A Twin-Candidate Based Approach for Event Pronoun Resolution using Composite Kernel
abstract: Treats event-pronoun resolution as selection among candidate verbal event antecedents and learns pairwise preferences between competing antecedent candidates, including cases with no suitable antecedent.

title: Resolving Event Noun Phrases to Their Verbal Mentions
abstract: Studies resolution of event-denoting noun phrases to earlier verbal mentions across potentially long discourse distances, using lexical, syntactic, morphological, semantic, and positional evidence for antecedent selection.

title: Joint Learning for Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Jointly models event coreference with event anaphoricity determination, providing transferable methods for deciding whether an event mention has a supported antecedent before antecedent selection.

title: Constrained Multi-Task Learning for Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Uses constrained multi-task learning for event coreference together with related subtasks including event anaphoricity determination, providing transferable machinery for no-link decisions and antecedent-oriented event resolution.

title: The More Antecedents, the Merrier: Resolving Multi-Antecedent Anaphors
abstract: Addresses anaphoric expressions whose interpretation depends on multiple antecedents and develops a model that can recover sets of antecedent mentions rather than forcing every anaphor to select a single antecedent.

title: Free the Plural: Unrestricted Split-Antecedent Anaphora Resolution
abstract: Develops end-to-end split-antecedent resolution without relying on gold identification of plural anaphors, allowing one anaphoric expression to be linked to multiple separately introduced antecedents.

title: Stay Together: A System for Single and Split-antecedent Anaphora Resolution
abstract: Provides a unified end-to-end architecture for single- and split-antecedent anaphora using predicted mentions, demonstrating how reference resolution can represent both ordinary and multi-antecedent links.

title: Scoring Coreference Chains with Split-Antecedent Anaphors
abstract: Generalizes coreference evaluation metrics to structures containing split antecedents; the resulting framework supports evaluation of multi-antecedent plural reference and has also been applied in shared-task settings involving discourse deixis.
